answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake that is slashed if the identity misbehaves, like a harbour charging every vessel to tie up at the jetty: a single honest agent pays once, but an attacker spawning thousands of sock-puppets must fund every berth, so the cost of the voyage scales with the size of the fake fleet. The stake also creates a narrow inlet — identities must pass through one verifiable, costly gate — so cheap mass creation stops paying for itself while genuine participants pass through once.
